questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Object Oriented Programming
questions.text: Compare Procedure Oriented Programming (POP) vs Object Oriented Programming (OOP) in terms of data security, modularity, top-down vs bottom-up approach, and code reusability.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Object Oriented Programming
questions.text: Explain core OOP features: Encapsulation, Data Abstraction, Inheritance, and Polymorphism with real-world examples.
What is a Reference Variable in C++? Compare Reference Variable vs Pointer with code snippets and memory models.

Explain Default Arguments in C++ functions. What are the rules for defining default arguments? Write a C++ function `calculateSimpleInterest(principal, time, rate=10.5)` demonstrating default arguments.
What is an Inline Function? How does the compiler handle inline function calls? In which situations will the C++ compiler ignore the `inline` request?

Explain Dynamic Memory Allocation in C++ using `new` and `delete` operators. Compare `new`/`delete` vs `malloc()`/`free()`. Write a program to allocate dynamic memory for an array of $N$ floats, sort them, and deallocate memory.

What is Function Overloading? Explain the rules and causes of ambiguity (e.g. default arguments, type conversion). Write overloaded functions `power(int base, int exp)` and `power(double base, int exp)`.
Explain `const` Member Functions, `const` Objects, and `mutable` data members with examples.
What is a Constructor? Explain Default, Parameterized, and Copy Constructors. Write a C++ program for a `Complex` class demonstrating all three types of constructors.
What is a Destructor? Explain object destruction order for automatic, static, and dynamically allocated objects.
Explain Deep Copy vs Shallow Copy in C++. Why is a user-defined Copy Constructor necessary when a class contains dynamically allocated pointer members? Write code illustrating shallow vs deep copy.
Explain Static Data Members and Static Member Functions. Write a C++ program where class `Account` uses a static variable to assign unique auto-incremented account numbers to each new object.

What is a Friend Function and Friend Class? Explain situations where friendship is useful. Write a program to add two private distance data members from class `DM` (meters and centimeters) and `DB` (feet and inches) using a friend function.
What is the `this` pointer in C++? Explain method chaining (`obj.setA(5).setB(10)`) using `return *this;`.
Explain Array of Objects and Passing/Returning Objects to/from Member Functions. Write a C++ program for a `Matrix` class to add two matrices using member function `Matrix add(Matrix m)`.
Explain Object Delegation and Containership (HAS-A relationship) vs Inheritance (IS-A relationship).
What is Operator Overloading? What are operators that cannot be overloaded in C++ (`.`, `.*`, `::`, `?:`, `sizeof`)? Overload unary `++` in both prefix and postfix forms for a `Counter` class.
Write a C++ program to overload binary `+` operator to concatenate two user-defined `String` class objects and `==` operator to compare them.
Overload binary `*` operator to multiply two `Matrix` objects using member function and check for dimensional validity.

Explain why the Stream Insertion (`<<`) and Stream Extraction (`>>`) operators must be overloaded as Friend Functions and not as member functions. Write a complete C++ program to overload `<<` and `>>` for a `Date` or `Time` class.

Explain Data Type Conversion: (a) Basic type to Class type (Constructor method), (b) Class type to Basic type (Casting Operator function `operator typename()`), (c) Class type to Another Class type. Write a program to convert `Celsius` class object to `Fahrenheit` class object.
Write a C++ program to convert coordinates from `Polar` system $(r, \theta)$ to `Cartesian` rectangular system $(x, y)$ using type conversion routine in destination class.
Overload Subscript operator `[]` for a safe array class that performs array index boundary checking.
Overload Function Call operator `()` and Assignment operator `=` with deep copy logic.
Explain types of Inheritance in C++: Single, Multilevel, Multiple, Hierarchical, and Hybrid Inheritance with syntax and UML diagrams.
Explain access control in inheritance (`public`, `protected`, `private` derivation) in a tabular format showing accessibility of base class members in derived class and outside class.

Explain Ambiguity in Multiple and Hybrid Inheritance (Diamond Problem). How does `virtual base class` eliminate multiple duplicate copies of the grandparent class? Write a complete C++ program for `Student` -> `Test`, `Sports` -> `Result` demonstrating virtual base class.
Explain Constructor and Destructor invocation order in multiple and multilevel inheritance. How are arguments passed to base class parameterized constructors from a derived class constructor?

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Virtual Functions and Dynamic Polymorphism
questions.text: What is Early Binding (Static Binding) vs Late Binding (Dynamic Binding)? Explain Virtual Functions and Runtime Polymorphism. Explain the internal working of Virtual Table (`vtable`) and Virtual Table Pointer (`vptr`).

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Virtual Functions and Dynamic Polymorphism
questions.text: Create an abstract base class `Media` with pure virtual functions `display()` and `read()`. Derive classes `Book` (with pages) and `Tape` (with playing time). Write a C++ program to demonstrate runtime polymorphism using base class pointers.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Virtual Functions and Dynamic Polymorphism
questions.text: What is a Pure Virtual Function? What is an Abstract Base Class? Why can we not create objects of an abstract class?

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Virtual Functions and Dynamic Polymorphism
questions.text: What is a Virtual Destructor? Explain why a base class destructor must be declared `virtual` when derived class objects are deleted using a base class pointer.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Virtual Functions and Dynamic Polymorphism
questions.text: What is Object Slicing in C++? How can object slicing be avoided using pointers or references?

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Virtual Functions and Dynamic Polymorphism
questions.text: Explain Run-Time Type Identification (RTTI): `typeid` operator and `dynamic_cast` operator with code examples.
What are Templates in C++? Explain Function Templates and Template Specialization. Write a template function `findMax(T a, T b)` to find maximum between two integers, floats, and characters.
Write a generic Class Template `Stack<T>` with member functions `push()`, `pop()`, and `display()` that works for integer, float, and character data types.
Explain Class Templates with Multiple Parameters (`template <class T1, class T2>`). Write a class template `Pair<T1, T2>` to store and display two different types of values.
Explain Exception Handling in C++: `try`, `catch`, and `throw`. Write a C++ program to handle Divide-by-Zero exception.
Explain Multiple Catch Blocks and Catch-All handler (`catch(...)`). What is Exception Specification (`throw(int, char)`) and Rethrowing an Exception?
Create a custom user-defined Exception class `NegativeNumberException` and throw it when a negative number is entered for calculating square root.

Explain the C++ Stream Class Hierarchy (`ios`, `istream`, `ostream`, `iostream`, `ifstream`, `ofstream`, `fstream`). Explain standard I/O manipulators (`setw()`, `setprecision()`, `setfill()`, `endl`).
Explain File Opening Modes (`ios::in`, `ios::out`, `ios::app`, `ios::binary`, `ios::ate`, `ios::trunc`). Explain File Pointers and positioning functions: `seekg()`, `seekp()`, `tellg()`, `tellp()`.
Write a C++ program to write an array of 5 `Student` objects (`roll`, `name`, `percentage`) to a binary file `student.dat` using `write()` and read them back using `read()`.
Write a C++ program to update a specific student record in a binary file `student.dat` given the roll number using random access (`seekg()`, `seekp()`).
Explain Error Handling in File I/O: `eof()`, `fail()`, `bad()`, `good()`, `clear()` member functions with examples.
Explain the components of Standard Template Library (STL): Containers (Vector, List, Deque, Map, Set), Iterators, and Algorithms. Compare `std::vector` vs `std::list`.
Write a C++ program using `std::vector` to store student marks, sort them in descending order using `std::sort()`, and find the highest mark using `std::max_element()`.
Explain `std::map` container in STL. Write a program using `std::map<string, int>` to store country names and their populations and search for a country.
Explain Function Objects (Functors) and Lambda Expressions in modern C++ with code snippets.
